q: Prime Minister elected by
ans: National Assembly of Pakistan, from among its members
facts: • The Prime Minister is elected by the National Assembly from among its members.
The President is elected by an electoral college that includes Parliament and provincial assemblies.

q: Why children are sent to school
ans: Duplicate of Q3: education, learning, social development and skills
facts: • Duplicate of Q3; replace with a clearer educational-purpose question.
• Duplicate of Q38.

q: Currency of Russia
facts: • Russian ruble (RUB), not rubble.

q: First woman in Pakistan Air Force
ans: Ayesha Farooq was reported as Pakistan’s first female fighter pilot qualified for combat duty; not the first woman in every PAF role
facts: • Ayesha Farooq was reported as Pakistan's first female fighter pilot to qualify for combat duty, not the first woman in the entire Air Force; other women served earlier in different roles.
Ayesha Farooq became known as Pakistan’s first female fighter pilot qualified for combat duty.
Women had served in other PAF roles before this milestone.

q: President elected by
ans: Electoral college: both Houses of Parliament plus the four Provincial Assemblies
facts: • Electoral college comprises both Houses of Parliament and the four Provincial Assemblies; not the National Assembly alone.
The President’s electoral college includes the Senate, National Assembly and four Provincial Assemblies.
It is not just a joint sitting of the National Assembly.

q: Why milk is boiled
ans: Duplicate of Q5: heating reduces harmful microbes; safe pasteurized milk may not require boiling
facts: • Duplicate of Q5; heating reduces microbes, but pasteurized milk does not always need boiling if handled safely.

q: Battle of Badr Hijri year
facts: • Duplicate of Q19.

q: Hazrat Hamza relation to Prophet Muhammad
ans: Paternal uncle and foster-brother, not maternal uncle
facts: • Hamza was the Prophet's paternal uncle and foster-brother, not maternal uncle.
Hamza (RA) was the Prophet’s paternal uncle and foster-brother.
He was martyred at the Battle of Uhud.

q: Badshahi Mosque location
facts: • Exam angle: learn the spelling, date/name and the related institution or location.
If the question is date-sensitive or wording-dependent, recheck the official source before the test.

q: Pakistan coastline
facts: • Duplicate of Q94; define measurement source.

q: Currency of Cuba
facts: • Duplicate of Q53; CUP is the official currency since the 2021 monetary unification.

q: Longest river in Asia
ans: Yangtze River (commonly cited as Asia’s longest)
facts: • Commonly accepted answer; length estimates vary.

q: Yellow Sea source
ans: The Yellow Sea supports important fisheries; “fishing” is broadly true but not a uniquely defining answer
facts: • The Yellow Sea supports fisheries, but this is not a unique geographic fact; rewrite as a more precise question.
The Yellow Sea lies between mainland China and the Korean Peninsula.
It supports fisheries and important shipping routes; “fishing” is too broad as a unique answer.

q: Abdul Qadir was a well-known player of which sport?
facts: • Abdul Qadir was a Pakistani leg-spin bowler known for reviving attacking leg-spin.
He played international cricket for Pakistan mainly from the late 1970s through the 1990s.

q: What was the original name of Prophet Yaqub (AS)?
facts: • In Islamic tradition, Prophet Yaqub (AS) is also called Isra'il.
Bani Isra'il means the Children of Israel and is a recurring term in the Qur'an.

q: Where will the next ICC Men's ODI Cricket World Cup be held?
facts: • The ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2027 runs from 2 October to 21 November 2027.
The 2027 event is jointly hosted by three African countries; the question must specify ODI/men's cricket because other World Cups have different hosts. Primary / official reference

q: When did the English East India Company first arrive at Surat?
ans: 1608 is commonly cited; 24 August is often given for the arrival of Captain William Hawkins's expedition in India
facts: • The East India Company was chartered in 1600 by Queen Elizabeth I.
Early company activity at Surat preceded the later establishment of British territorial rule.

q: Jinnah's Fourteen Points were presented in response to which report?
ans: The Nehru Report (1928); Jinnah announced his Fourteen Points in 1929
facts: • The points defended Muslim political safeguards and federal arrangements.
The Nehru Report proposed a constitutional framework for British India and became a major point of disagreement.

q: Which word is intended by the dictionary-order question in the source?
ans: The supplied key says “Academic”; the question wording is incomplete, so confirm against the original options
facts: • Dictionary order compares letters from left to right.
Without the full options, it is not possible to confirm that “Academic” is the first word in the intended list.

q: Who developed an early practical solar cell?
facts: • Fritts made an early selenium-based photovoltaic cell.
Modern silicon solar cells were developed later, including the 1954 Bell Labs cell.

q: Who accompanied Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) during the Hijrah to Madinah?
facts: • The migration took place in 622 CE and marks the beginning of the Hijri calendar era.
The two stayed in the Cave of Thawr before continuing toward Madinah.

q: What is the capital of Venezuela?
facts: • Caracas is Venezuela's capital and largest urban centre.
Venezuela is in northern South America and has a Caribbean coastline.

q: In which Hijri year was the Battle of Uhud fought?
facts: • Uhud was fought near Madinah.
The Muslim force initially numbered about 1,000; around 300 withdrew before the battle, leaving about 700.

q: Who is the Supreme Commander of Pakistan's Armed Forces?
ans: The President of Pakistan, Asif Ali Zardari (as of 14 October 2026)
facts: • Pakistan's Constitution assigns the President the role of Supreme Commander.
The President's constitutional role is distinct from the operational command exercised by the military leadership. Primary / official reference

q: Where is OPEC headquartered?
facts: • OPEC was founded in Baghdad in September 1960.
OPEC's member countries coordinate petroleum policies; it is not the same organization as OPEC+.

q: What is another name for the Manila Pact?
ans: Southeast Asia Collective Defense Treaty (the Manila Pact)
facts: • It was signed in Manila on 8 September 1954.
SEATO was the organization associated with the treaty and was dissolved in 1977.

q: In which Pakistani river is the Indus river dolphin found?
facts: • The Indus river dolphin is a freshwater cetacean and is endangered.
Its main range is in Pakistan's Indus River system, with a small related population in India's Beas River.

q: What does “Tanzil” mean?
facts: • In Qur'anic usage, Tanzil refers to revelation or sending down of divine scripture.
“Wahy” is the broader Arabic term for divine revelation.

q: How many Nishan-e-Haider recipients are commonly listed?
facts: • Nishan-e-Haider is Pakistan's highest military gallantry award.
Several awards relate to the 1947–48, 1965, 1971 and 1999 conflicts; spellings and lists should be checked against official sources.

q: Who wrote Tafsir al-Tabari?
facts: • Al-Tabari was a major Muslim historian and Qur'anic commentator of the 9th–10th centuries.
The work is also known as Jami' al-Bayan.

q: What is the approximate length of the Indus River?
facts: • The Indus rises in the Tibetan Plateau and flows through Ladakh and Pakistan to the Arabian Sea.
Pakistan's major barrages and irrigation networks depend heavily on the Indus system.

q: What is the approximate length of the Amazon River?
ans: About 6,400 km; estimates vary by source and headwater definition
facts: • The Amazon has the world's largest river discharge by volume.
Whether it is longer than the Nile depends on the measurement method and source chosen.

q: Who wrote the Urdu novel “Raja Gidh”?
facts: • “Raja Gidh” is a celebrated Urdu novel first published in 1981.
Bano Qudsia was also known for her television and stage writing.

q: Where is Data Ganj Bakhsh's shrine located?
facts: • Data Ganj Bakhsh is the honorific of Ali Hujwiri, a Sufi scholar.
His major work is “Kashf-ul-Mahjoob,” an early Persian Sufi text.

q: In which Hijri year was the Battle of Uhud fought?
facts: • The battle followed the Muslim victory at Badr in 2 AH.
Hazrat Hamza (RA) was martyred at Uhud.

q: What is the capital of France?
facts: • Paris is the capital and largest city of France.
France is a member of the European Union and a permanent member of the UN Security Council.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam present his Fourteen Points?
facts: • Jinnah's Fourteen Points were a response to the Nehru Report of 1928.
They demanded safeguards for Muslim representation and provincial autonomy.

q: When and where was the All-India Muslim League founded?
facts: • The founding meeting took place during the annual session of the All-India Muhammadan Educational Conference.
Nawab Salimullah, Viqar-ul-Mulk, and other Muslim leaders were central to its formation.

q: Who became the first permanent president of the All-India Muslim League?
ans: Aga Khan III (elected permanent president in 1908)
facts: • The Muslim League was founded in 1906; its early leadership included Nawab Viqar-ul-Mulk.
Some sources simplify the first presidency to Aga Khan III, so “first permanent president” is the clearest wording.

q: On what date did Israel declare independence?
facts: • The declaration was made in Tel Aviv before the British Mandate ended.
The date is observed as Israel's Independence Day according to the Hebrew calendar.

q: Who is the President of France (as of October 2026)?
facts: • Macron began his second presidential term in May 2022.
The French president is elected for a five-year term.

q: What is the deepest known point in the ocean?
ans: Challenger Deep, in the Mariana Trench (about 10.9 km deep)
facts: • The Mariana Trench is in the western Pacific Ocean.
Challenger Deep is deeper than Mount Everest is high above sea level.

q: Who is regarded as the founder of modern nursing?
facts: • Nightingale became prominent during the Crimean War.
International Nurses Day is observed on 12 May, her birthday.

q: Which country holds the G20 presidency in 2026?
facts: • The United States assumed the 2026 G20 presidency on 1 December 2025.
The 2026 G20 Leaders' Summit is scheduled for Miami, Florida; G20 presidency rotates annually. Primary / official reference

q: Where is the headquarters of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)?
facts: • The OIC was founded in 1969 following the first Islamic Summit in Rabat, Morocco.
It is an intergovernmental organization of member states from the Muslim world and beyond.

q: Was the OIC founded by one country or by several countries?
ans: It was established collectively by participating states at the 1969 Rabat Islamic Summit; no single country founded it alone
facts: • The first summit followed an arson attack on Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem.
The organization's headquarters is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

q: What is the currency of Cuba?
facts: • Cuba ended its dual-currency system in 2021.
The Cuban peso is abbreviated CUP.

q: Which Pakistani city is often cited as one of the hottest?
ans: Jacobabad, Sindh (often cited; “hottest city” depends on period and metric)
facts: • Jacobabad has recorded extreme summer temperatures.
A record high on a single day is different from the highest annual or average temperature.

q: What is the world's second-largest continent by area?
facts: • Asia is the largest continent, followed by Africa.
Africa is crossed by the Equator and both the Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn.

q: When did Salah become obligatory for Muslims?
ans: During the Mi'raj, before the Hijrah; often placed around the 10th/12th year of Prophethood in traditional chronologies
facts: • The five daily prayers are obligatory in Islamic belief.
Exact Gregorian/Hijri dating of the Mi'raj is not universally agreed.

q: What is commonly cited as Pakistan's largest artificial lake/reservoir?
ans: Keenjhar Lake (Kalri Lake), Thatta District, Sindh
facts: • The Sindh Irrigation Department describes Keenjhar as an artificially created reservoir formed by embankments using natural depressions.

It is a major water source for Karachi; Manchar Lake is commonly described as Pakistan's largest natural freshwater lake. Primary / official reference PRO GENIUS FORCES ACADEMY | PMA LONG COURSE Page 14

q: What is the world's largest lake by surface area?
facts: • Although named a sea, the Caspian is an enclosed inland body of water.
Lake Baikal is the world's deepest lake and holds a large share of the world's unfrozen surface freshwater.

q: What is the height of Mount Everest?
facts: • Nepal and China announced this jointly recognized height in 2020.
Everest is the world's highest mountain above sea level.

q: Which pass connects Quetta with Sibi?
facts: • The Bolan Pass is a historic route through the Toba Kakar Range in Balochistan.
It has long linked the Quetta region with the plains toward Sibi and beyond.

q: In which city is Nishtar Hospital located?
facts: • Nishtar Hospital is a major teaching hospital associated with Nishtar Medical University.
Multan is often called the City of Saints.

q: Which corridor separates Pakistan from Tajikistan?
ans: The Wakhan Corridor of Afghanistan; the original wording “separates Pakistan from the Middle East” is incorrect
facts: • The Wakhan Corridor is a narrow strip of northeastern Afghanistan.
It separates Pakistan's northern border region from Tajikistan and reaches toward China.

q: Over approximately how many years was the Qur'an revealed?
facts: • Revelation began in Makkah and continued until shortly before the Prophet's death.
The first revealed verses are traditionally identified as Qur'an 96:1–5.

q: Which Companion was a son-in-law of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
ans: Hazrat Ali (RA), who married Fatimah (RA); Uthman (RA) was also a son-in-law
facts: • Ali and Fatimah's children included Hasan and Husayn (RA).
Uthman (RA) married two of the Prophet's daughters in succession, which earned him the title Dhun-Nurayn in Islamic tradition.

q: Which constitution of Pakistan introduced a presidential system in 1962?
facts: • It was introduced under President Ayub Khan.
It was replaced by the Constitution of 1973, which established a parliamentary federal system.

q: What is the currency of Libya?
facts: • The Libyan dinar replaced the Libyan pound in 1971.
Tripoli is Libya's capital.

q: What is the world's deepest lake?
facts: • Baikal reaches about 1,642 m at its deepest point.
It is also one of the world's oldest lakes and contains exceptional freshwater biodiversity.

q: Where and when were the first Asian Games held?
facts: • The first Asian Games opened on 4 March 1951.
The event is organized under the Olympic Council of Asia.

q: In which Pakistani province is the Cholistan Desert?
facts: • Cholistan is locally also known as Rohi.
It adjoins the Thar Desert region toward the southeast.

q: What is the largest city in Sindh by population?
facts: • Karachi is Pakistan's largest city and a major seaport and financial centre.
It is the capital of Sindh province, while Hyderabad is another major Sindhi city.

q: When was the first Nobel Prize awarded?
facts: • The first Nobel Prizes were awarded in Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine, Literature, and Peace.
The Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences was added later, in 1969.

q: Which angel is called Ruh-ul-Qudus in the Qur'anic/Islamic tradition?
facts: • Jibreel is traditionally identified as the angel who conveyed revelation to the prophets.
“Ruh al-Amin” is another Qur'anic expression associated with the trustworthy spirit.

q: What was the relationship between Asma bint Abu Bakr (RA) and Zubair ibn al-Awwam (RA)?
facts: • Their son Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr became a prominent early Muslim figure.
Asma was the daughter of Abu Bakr (RA) and the sister of Aisha (RA).

q: What is one quarter of one tenth of 120?
facts: • One tenth of 120 is 12, and one quarter of 12 is 3.
Read chained fractions from the inside: 120 ÷ 10 ÷ 4.

q: Who was the President of Cuba during the Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962?
ans: Osvaldo Dorticós Torrado (formal President); Fidel Castro was Prime Minister and revolutionary leader
facts: • The Cuban Missile Crisis occurred in October 1962.
The crisis involved the Soviet Union, Cuba and the United States.

q: Which battle is often listed as the second major battle after Badr?
ans: Battle of Uhud (3 AH), in common simplified GK lists; sequencing varies with whether expeditions are counted
facts: • Uhud took place near Madinah in 625 CE.
For “second Ghazwa” the question must specify the textbook's counting convention because early expeditions are counted differently.

q: In which battle was Hazrat Hamza (RA) martyred?
facts: • Hamza (RA) was the Prophet's paternal uncle and foster-brother.
Islamic historical accounts name Wahshi ibn Harb as the person who killed him at Uhud.
